transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Yeah, thanks. Um, I'm here because things just got completely out of hand at work. I'm an industrial production manager, and I went from launching these nonstop plant redesign projects—which, honestly, the floor layout was a total disaster before I took over. The previous manager, Dave, he had absolutely no idea what he was doing with the assembly line space. I actually brought in some optimization models from my grad program to try and fix the bottlenecks, which was fascinating, really. 

So I was doing all that, calling our steel suppliers way after hours, just totally rewriting the entire shift plan by myself. I'd be on the phone in my kitchen for hours. My kitchen is so tiny, by the way, I really need to move out of that apartment because the plumbing keeps making this weird humming noise every time the upstairs neighbor showers, and it drives my cat insane. 

But... right, anyway, I was doing all these massive overhauls, and then... suddenly, I just couldn't do it anymore. I became completely unable to keep up with the very plans I had just set in motion. It's like I just completely crashed, and I don't even know how to face my team right now.
Has anything like this ever happened to you before, where you went from being highly productive to suddenly being unable to keep up?

Um... before? I don't really know. I can't quite remember if it's ever happened exactly like this. I mean, maybe back when I was finishing my master's thesis? I was working crazy hours then too, but my advisor was just... well, he was this guy, Dr. Aris, who was absolutely obsessed with supply chain logistics in the automotive industry. 

He drove this ancient Volvo, actually, one of those boxy ones from the nineties that look like a toaster? He swore it was the most reliable car ever made, but it broke down in the faculty parking lot at least three times a semester. I actually had to help him jump-start it once when it was pouring rain. My umbrella completely flipped inside out, and it was one of those really nice golf umbrellas I got from a vendor conference in Chicago. Chicago is so windy, they aren't kidding about the nickname, though honestly the deep dish pizza totally makes up for it. I tried making deep dish at home once in my cast iron skillet, but the crust just got totally soggy because I think I used the wrong kind of crushed tomatoes. You really have to get the San Marzano ones, but they're always sold out at my local grocery store... 

But, um, wait, what were you asking? Oh, about crashing. Yeah, I'm just... I'm really not sure if I've had this specific thing happen before.
Can you recall if you’ve ever had a period of time before this where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning for at least two weeks?

Well, um, feeling down... yeah, lately, definitely. It's like... I wake up in my temporary apartment, and there's just this heavy, hollow feeling sitting right in my chest. It's like the whole day is already completely ruined before I even get in my car to drive to the plant. And speaking of my car, the heater has been acting up, which is just brilliant timing because it was freezing this morning. I had to scrape ice off the windshield with a plastic spatula from my kitchen because I couldn't find my ice scraper. I think I left it in Dave's truck—the old manager, remember?—when he helped me move some boxes into this apartment. 

Which, by the way, this temporary place is supposed to be "fully furnished," but the couch feels like it's stuffed with cinder blocks. I tried putting a mattress pad over the cushions, but it just slides right off every time my cat jumps on it. My cat, Mr. Whiskers, he's been so needy lately, just meowing at the door all night. I think he misses the old place, or maybe he just hates the smell of the hallway here. The hallway always smells like boiled cabbage and cheap air freshener. It's a really specific, terrible combination. I actually bought one of those fancy essential oil diffusers to try and drown it out, the kind that changes colors? But the blue light on it is so bright it keeps me awake, which I really don't need right now because I'm already so tired... 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, feeling down for two weeks. Yeah, lately, it's just that heavy, hollow feeling every single morning. I don't know about before this, though. It's just... really bad right now.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this current one where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks at a time?

Um, before this current one? I mean, this whole heavy, depressed stretch right now has been going on for about three months. It really started dragging me down right around the time I got this plant assignment and had to move. Moving is just the absolute worst, isn't it? I had to pack up all my books, and I have this massive collection of historical biographies. I was reading this fascinating one about Catherine the Great—did you know she actually had a roller coaster built in her gardens? Well, they called them ice slides back then, but it's basically the same concept. 

Anyway, the movers totally mishandled the box with my favorite hardcovers. One of the guys, I think his name was Steve, he was wearing these really worn-out work boots that left scuff marks all over the hardwood floors of my old place. I spent two hours trying to buff them out with a tennis ball on a stick. It's this trick I learned from a janitor back in undergrad. You just cut a little slit in a tennis ball and stick it on a broom handle... works like magic, honestly, but it completely destroyed my shoulders. 

But yeah, this heavy feeling... it's been about three months now. The move and the new plant just made it so much harder to manage. I just feel so drained by it all.
Have you ever had any other periods in your life, before this current one lasting three months, where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Um, before this current one? I... I really don't think so. I can't remember ever feeling this stuck for this long before. I mean, sure, I've had bad days, like anyone, especially when production quotas are coming up. Last year, we had this massive supply chain issue with the aluminum casings, and the supplier was just completely dodging my calls. It was this guy named Greg, and he always sounded like he was eating something really crunchy on the phone. Like chips or maybe carrots? It was so distracting. I actually started buying these artisanal kettle chips after that because it made me crave them, the jalapeño flavored ones. They are so spicy, though, I always have to drink a huge glass of milk afterward. But I'm lactose intolerant, so I have to buy the oat milk, which is fine, but it just doesn't have the same mouthfeel, you know? It's a little too watery for my taste, especially in coffee. I tried making an oat milk latte at home with this little frother wand I got online, but it just splattered everywhere and stained my favorite white blouse. 

But um, no, I don't think I've ever had a period like this before where I felt this down for weeks at a time. This is pretty new.

Have you ever had any episodes in your life before this current one — even just one week or more — where you felt down or uninterested in things nearly every day, to the point where it affected your work or daily life?

Even just a week? Um... no. Honestly, no. I mean, I've taken a week off work before, but that was just for vacation. Like, a couple of years ago I rented this cabin near the lake because I wanted to completely unplug. But the Wi-Fi there was actually completely dead, not just slow, like, non-existent. Which wouldn't have been a big deal, except I had just bought this automatic smart-feeder for Mr. Whiskers, and it required a constant internet connection to dispense the kibble. 

I had this pet sitter checking in on him—her name was Chloe, she was taking a gap year to do ceramics—and she had to manually feed him anyway. She kept texting me these really blurry photos of her pottery instead of my cat, which was... weird. The bowls were nice, I guess, lots of terracotta and this really pretty moss green glaze. I actually bought a moss green bath mat for this new apartment because I read green is supposed to lower your heart rate. But the material is so cheap, it just sheds everywhere. Every time I get out of the shower, my wet feet are just covered in green fuzz, like I've been walking through a swamp or something. It's so frustrating because I specifically ordered the one that said 'anti-shed' in the description, and returning things online is such a hassle because you have to print the label, and I don't even own a printer anymore...

But um, what were we... oh, right. No, I haven't ever felt down like this before, not even for a week. This is really the first time it's ever messed with my daily life like this.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had any times in your life, even just a few days long, where you felt persistently sad or uninterested in things?

Even just a few days? Um... no. I really don't think so. I mean, sometimes I'll have a weekend where I just don't feel like doing anything, but that's usually just because I'm exhausted from the week. Like when we had that audit last month, I literally just slept all day Saturday. But I woke up Sunday and felt fine, well, mostly fine, except my neck was completely stiff because I fell asleep on the couch. 

It's this awful faux-leather couch that came with the apartment. It's that weird brown color that tries to look like vintage leather but just ends up looking like mud. And it's so sticky in the summer. I tried putting a throw blanket over it, this really nice chunky knit one I got at a craft fair, but the yarn snagged on my watch and just unraveled. It was a complete disaster. The woman who made it was so sweet, though. She had this little booth set up with all these hand-dyed yarns, and she was telling me about how she uses avocado pits to get this really soft pink color. I tried it at home once, boiling the pits, but it just made my whole kitchen smell like hot garbage and the fabric I tried to dye just came out looking kind of... dirty? 

But um, no, not even for a few days. I've never felt this kind of... heavy, empty feeling before this current stretch. It's just so new and weird for me.
Have you ever had any times in your life before this current period — even just a day or two — where you felt persistently sad or uninterested in things?

A day or two? Um... no. I mean, just normal bad days, I guess, like anyone has. Like if things go wrong at the plant. Last month I had this awful Tuesday because they made management do this mandatory compliance training on Zoom. It was eight hours long, and the presenter had this virtual background of the Golden Gate Bridge, but the lighting was so weird that every time he leaned forward, his ears would just disappear into the bridge cables. It was incredibly distracting. 

I tried to message my coworker about it, but I accidentally sent it to the general chat. Which was mortifying, but honestly, nobody was paying attention anyway because the audio kept echoing. It sounded like he was broadcasting from inside a tin can. I actually buy these imported crushed tomatoes that come in tin cans—the San Marzano ones—for when I make pasta sauce. You're supposed to crush them by hand, which is supposedly better for the texture, but the tomato juice always gets under my fingernails and it looks like I've been digging in the dirt. I tried wearing those yellow dish gloves once, but they make my hands sweat so much, and they have that weird rubbery smell that just lingers on your skin for days, no matter how much you wash them. I even bought this fancy lavender and oatmeal soap from a farmer's market to try and get rid of the smell, but it just made my hands smell like rubber and flowers, which is honestly worse...

But, um, what were you asking? A day of feeling sad? No. I've never had a day or two of feeling empty or down like this before. It's just never happened to me until now.
